response: Causal chain: (1) the instruction is present at system level -> (2) the agent writes tests derived from each stated behavior before implementing -> (3) spec clauses become executable checks while attention on the spec is highest -> (4) implementation iterates until self-tests pass -> (5) held-out grader tests overlap the self-tests enough that pass rate rises. The chain has two fragile links. Link 2 is compliance: a small model may implement first anyway; only transcript inspection can confirm test-first ordering happened. Link 5 is fidelity: self-tests encode the agent's reading of the spec, so a systematic misreading produces confident wrongness the grader still catches (shared blindspot). Supporting evidence needed: (a) paired A/B trials with held-out grading showing a positive pass-rate delta; (b) transcript-level confirmation that candidate arms wrote tests before code in most trials; (c) turn-count comparison showing the arm does not lose trials to the turn cap, which would confound overhead with reasoning failure. Disconfirming evidence: candidate arms hitting turn limits materially more often, or self-tests that pass while graders fail on the same clause, which would localize the failure to fidelity rather than coverage.
